title: Your neighborhood
hookLine: add more water to the broth, for the neighbors: the Prophet's kitchen advice and Islam's teaching that neighbors have rights
tomorrow: why does the Torah keep saying: you were strangers?

lines: ADD MORE WATER TO THE BROTH.
cards: Onions and garlic in a pot, and the smell drifting under a door and down the hall. Whoever lives next to that kitchen smells a dinner they won't eat.
In a hadith, a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, recorded in Sahih Muslim, he gives his companion Abu Dharr a kitchen instruction. When you cook a broth, add more water to it.
Then look to your neighbors, and give them some.

teach.b: That kitchen line sits inside Islam's larger teaching on the neighbor.
The Quran lists the neighbor among those owed kindness, right beside parents, orphans and the needy, and it names two kinds: the neighbor who is kin, and the neighbor who is not.
Then a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, passed on by Aisha: the Prophet said the angel Gabriel kept urging him about the neighbor until he thought the neighbor would be made an heir. Not an heir in law.
A way of saying your neighbor has a claim on you, close to family.
Another hadith goes further: someone whose neighbor isn't safe from his harm is not a true believer. In some Muslim homes, this lives on in plates.
A dish goes next door, and when the plate comes back, it doesn't come back empty. So the neighbor in Islam isn't just whoever happens to live nearby.
It's a relationship with rights. And it starts with things you can smell and taste: a pot with a little extra water, a plate that goes back full.

how: Muslims learn the rights of the neighbor from the Quran (4:36) and the hadith. Some families honor them by sending food to the households next door, for example at Ramadan and Eid.

games.why: in Islam the neighbor is a relationship with rights on both sides, close to family. it starts with a name, not a complaint.

practice: For these two minutes, listen. Find the sounds of the people around you: a door, footsteps, a voice through the wall, a car pulling in. For each one, ask quietly: do I know that person's name?
Let the ones you don't know stay with you until the sit ends.

wordCard.voice: Your neighborhood: in Islamic teaching, the people around you have rights, close to family, from a share of the broth to safety from your harm.

orig.note: Arabic: neighbor. The Quran speaks of the neighbor who is kin and the neighbor who is not.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: neighbors, the ones the extra water in the broth was for. See you tomorrow.
